title: CI arg-validation leg inverts ANY non-zero exit — a harness crash on the bogus-arg path would be a false green, not just a silent accept
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml: "tools/harness.sh input-parity && [ -x ./bin/harness ] && ! ./bin/harness input-parity bogus >/dev/null 2>&1" with the comment above it: "the r3-N7 pin: a bogus arg must be REJECTED (usage exit 2) — if the validation ever silently accepts it (exit 0), the negation fails the gate. The `[ -x ]` guard keeps a missing binary a hard failure, never a false-green (127 would invert to 0)." — tools/ci-local.sh:63: "Input parity (T1 across inputs — mouse == touch == controller + CLI arg-validation leg)|tools/harness.sh input-parity && [ -x ./bin/harness ] && ! ./bin/harness input-parity bogus >/dev/null 2>&1" — harness/main.odin: "if len(rest) > 1 || (len(rest) == 1 && rest[0] != \"save\") { usage() }" and usage(): "os.exit(2)"
detail: The `!` leg inverts ANY non-zero exit to green — a crash (panic/segfault) on the bogus-arg path passes exactly like the intended usage-exit-2; only exit 0 fails the gate, yet the comment pins exit 2.
recommended_fix: Capture the exit code and require exactly 2: `./bin/harness input-parity bogus >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]` — rejects crashes (1/139) and silent accepts (0) alike.
